citation: Pham H, Trahair L, Phillips L, Rayner C, Horowitz M, Jones K. A randomized, crossover study of the acute effects of acarbose and gastric distension, alone and combined, on postprandial blood pressure in healthy older adults. BMC Geriatr. 2019;19.
protocol: After overnight fast, 300 mL drink of 100 g sucrose (about 407 kcal), with or without 100 mg acarbose; crossover with a 300 mL water preload arm; MAP and HR every 3 min to 120 min (baseline from -9 to -3 min); blood glucose at -2, 30, 60, 90, 120 min.
population: 10 healthy community-dwelling older adults (2 male, 8 female; age 74.0 +/- 1.4 y; BMI 26.2 +/- 1.1 kg/m2); no GI disease, diabetes, or significant cardiac, renal or respiratory disease. Three fainted during the study days.

reports.marker: mean arterial pressure (maximum fall and AUC)

note: The usable postprandial numbers are AUCs, maxima and baseline means (mean +/- SEM) in the Results text; the time-course means for MAP, HR, SMA flow and glucose are figure-only (Figures 2-4). MAP is printed, not SBP. Sucrose, not glucose: protocol kind set to other. n=10 for BP and HR, n=9 for glucose and flow.
